questions.prompt: Which of these expressions are TRUE (non-zero) in C?
questions.explain: In C, 0 is false and every other value is true. `-1` and `!0` (which is 1) are non-zero. The character constant `'0'` is the ASCII code 48, also non-zero. `NULL` is a null pointer, i.e. zero.
option_notes: Zero is the only false integer value.
Any non-zero value is true, negatives included.
`'0'` is the character whose code is 48, not the number 0.
A null pointer compares equal to 0, so it is false.

questions.prompt: In C, a false value is {{0}}; any other value is true.
questions.explain: There is no mandatory boolean type before C99 (and even `<stdbool.h>` only provides `bool`, `true`=1 and `false`=0 on top of integers).
